transition.heading: The Great Transition: From Shadows to Genesis
g.layperson: We used to think: 'Earth pulls the apple with a force depending on its mass.' Now we see: space has its own 'step' (L) and its 'beauty proportion' — the Golden Ratio (Φ² ≈ 2.618). Their product gives the acceleration of gravity. Mass is no longer the cause — it only bends space, while the acceleration is determined by geometry. The apple falls because space itself moves with this rhythm.
g.pro: Classical form: g = G·M / R². Gravitational constant G = 6.67430×10⁻¹¹ m³·kg⁻¹·s⁻², M — source mass (kg), R — distance (m). Genesis form: g = L · Φ². L = 3.747405725×10⁻⁹ m — fundamental vacuum length ('Pixel of Reality'). Φ² = 2.6180339887 — square of the Golden Ratio. Derived from g ≈ 9.811237 → L = g/Φ². Acceleration becomes a pure geometric constant. Vacuum eigenfrequency: f = c / L ≈ 8.00×10¹⁶ Hz.
e.layperson: Previously: E = M·c² — mass times speed of light squared. Now: energy is ħ (Planck's constant) × F (base frequency of the Universe) × N (number of 'ticks' in the object). Everything 'ticks' instead of 'weighs'. More ticks — more energy. Mass disappears, only rhythm remains.
e.pro: Classical: E = M·c², c = 299,792,458 m/s. Genesis: E = ħ · F · N. ħ = 1.054571817×10⁻³⁴ J·s, F = c / L ≈ 8.00×10¹⁶ Hz, N — integer quantum act count. For a body, N = M / m_node, where m_node = ħ/(c·L) ≈ 9.4×10⁻³⁵ kg. Energy is counting phase nodes: each contributes ħ·F, total N gives the full energy.
m.layperson: Classically mass is inertia: M = F / a. Now mass is simply the number of 'knots' in space: M = m_node · N. m_node — mass of one knot (~9.4×10⁻³⁵ kg), N — how many knots in the body. Matter is not solid stuff, but ripples on the vacuum fabric. More ripples (knots) — more mass.
m.pro: Classical inertia: M = F / a. Genesis: M = m_node · N. m_node = ħ/(c·L) ≈ 9.4×10⁻³⁵ kg — mass of a phase node. N = M / m_node (for 1 kg, N ≈ 1.06×10³⁴). Each node occupies a volume ~L³. Mass is a macroscopic effect of the synchronized count of these nodes. Inertia is resistance to changing the synchronization state.
